classification.difficultyReason: Translate the walking bearing into an interior angle, solve the resulting triangle while excluding the supplementary angle, then convert the angle at the starting point back into a true bearing and find the remaining side.

content.prompt: Sonia starts at $O$ and walks 600 metres due east to point $A$. She then walks on a bearing of $250^\circ\mathrm{T}$ to point $B$, 750 metres from $O$. Find:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the bearing of $B$ from $O$, correct to the nearest degree

answer.short:
$234^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

Use the sine rule to find the triangle's angles, then measure the bearing clockwise from north.
answer.worked:
The bearing of $O$ from $A$ is $270^\circ\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle OAB=270^\circ-250^\circ=20^\circ$. By the sine rule:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\angle OBA}{600}&=\frac{\sin20^\circ}{750}\\\sin\angle OBA&=\frac{600\sin20^\circ}{750}\\\angle OBA&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{600\sin20^\circ}{750}\right)\\\angle OBA&\approx15.8795606^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The supplementary alternative exceeds $160^\circ$, so it cannot accompany the $20^\circ$ angle in this triangle.
$$\begin{align*}\angle AOB&=180^\circ-20^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{600\sin20^\circ}{750}\right)\\\angle AOB&\approx144.1204394^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Since $B$ lies south of $OA$, its bearing from $O$ is:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=90^\circ+\angle AOB\\\text{Bearing}&\approx234.1204394^\circ\\\text{Bearing}&=234^\circ\mathrm{T}\quad\text{(nearest degree).}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: the distance from $A$ to $B$, correct to the nearest metre

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded value of $\angle AOB$ from part a. By the sine rule:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{\sin\angle AOB}&=\frac{750}{\sin20^\circ}\\AB&=\frac{750\sin\left(160^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{600\sin20^\circ}{750}\right)\right)}{\sin20^\circ}\\AB&\approx1285.1948068\text{ m}\\AB&=1285\text{ m}\quad\text{(nearest metre).}\end{align*}$$
